ethan_sales: Customer (AegisMed) asked whether we can support a fully disconnected POC and what the operational constraints are. Key asks: secure transfer, upgrade/rollback options, offline telemetry, licensing activation, and any legal/export constraints. Need short checklist to share.

maya_se: Yes we can. Quick checklist to communicate:
- transport options (USB courier, encrypted tape, controlled airgap via one-way transfer)
- bundle layout (bootstrap runtime + model chunks + manifest + SBOM + signatures)
- install pre-reqs (disk, RAM, supported kernel)
- upgrade cadence options (monthly model deltas, quarterly runtime patches)
- rollback strategy and snapshot requirements

priya_security: Add security items: all artifacts signed (Ed25519/ECDSA), manifest includes signing cert chain, SBOM in CycloneDX v1.4, signed attestations for provenance. Offline telemetry: only store locally unless customer allows manual log export. Also confirm any export-control classification for models (we need to run legal review).

leo_ops: Ops notes: estimate bandwidth and disk: for model size 320GB we need ~1.25x during staging so ~400GB free. If transfer is USB 2.0 vs USB3 matters for time. Example transfer times: USB3 (~5Gbps) ~10 minutes/100GB? (rough calc). Also: chunk size defaults to 256MB to allow resume; larger chunks reduce manifest length but increase re-transfer cost on failure.

ethan_sales: They asked about license activation without outbound internet. Options?

maya_se: Two options:
1) Signed offline token: we generate a signed license file tied to HW fingerprint (they provide host UUIDs). They place file at `/etc/redwood/license.json`. Agent validates signature locally.
2) HSM-assisted: they provide public key/HSM endpoint; we encrypt license blob to their key so only their HSM can decrypt during install.

priya_security: Also need process for emergency revocation. If a license must be revoked, we issue a signed revocation manifest and courier it to them; agent checks revocation manifest on scheduled checks. Document this in SOW.

leo_ops: Rollback: we require snapshots or btrfs/zfs snapshot support. Our agent will create pre-update snapshot and keep it for N days (configurable). Rolling back via agent is fast if snapshot present. Without snapshots, rollback is full reinstall from previous bundle (slower).

ops-bot: Reminder: package builder job 45321 queued for offline bundle generation. ETA ~48h. Artifact: offline-package-20240301-45321.tar.gz

ethan_sales: Anything legal/regulatory they should expect?

priya_security: Yes: export controls (model weights may be restricted), HIPAA concerns (PHI in logs), and contractual SLA for physical transfer. We'll need customer's SOC2/ISO docs for on-prem accesses.

maya_se: For minimal customer friction include: simple verify script and human-run checklist. Example verify snippet we can provide:```
#!/bin/sh
set -e
sha256sum -c bundle.manifest || { echo "checksum fail"; exit 1; }
./redwood-agent --verify-signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz || { echo "signature fail"; exit 2; }
```

leo_ops: Action items:
- Maya: produce bullet checklist + verify script sample (3 business days)
- Priya: fill security questionnaire entries and flag export-control items (2 business days)
- Ops: confirm disk/ram/GPU matrix and snapshot guidance (1 business day)
- Ethan: confirm courier window and whether they want host-fingerprint binding for license (today)

ethan_sales: I'll confirm courier window and host list today and loop in legal if export control looks hairy. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
